title: Common-unit comparison before the varying isomorphism
statement:
theorem diagonalTrace_finitePush_unit_common
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l X] [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l S]
    {f : X ⟶ S} (p : Presentation l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) f) :
    ((p.finitePushUnit l ≫
        p.Rf.R.map (p.coefficientsX.unitMap l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) p.LX)) ≫
        p.limits.iso.hom.app (p.restrictionX.F.mapDerivedCategory.obj
          (SpTowerClasses.unit X (SpTowerClasses.Arings l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) X)))) ≫
        p.LS.R.map (p.varying.inv.app
          (SpTowerClasses.unit X
            (SpTowerClasses.Arings l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) X))) =
      p.coefficientsS.unitMap l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) p.LS ≫
        p.LS.R.map (p.restrictionS.F.mapDerivedCategory.map
          ((SpTowerShriek.adjunction l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) p.base p.model.geometry).homEquiv _ _
            (p.model.coefficientPullback.derivedIso l (ULift.{u} (Padic l))).hom))

source.place: paragraph (2), ordinary coefficient-unit square before the varying comparison

proof.text: Prove the ordinary coefficient cone square. Faithful scalar forgetting and limit extensionality reduce it to finite constant coefficient sheaves; sheafification and integer generation reduce the normalized coefficient maps to their value on one.

Evaluate an exact square on a single complex in degree zero. Naturality of its cochain unit and of the exact single-functor comparisons gives the corresponding single-object square. Apply this to the completed coefficient pushforward.

Use restricted-push acyclicity to construct the full normalized varying square. On K-injectives its isomorphism agrees with the supplied varying comparison; K-injective resolutions and naturality extend that equality to every derived object. The canonical derived adjunction unit on a single object is the ordinary adjunct followed by the right-derived single comparison.

Expand the coefficient cone maps. Commute their single comparisons through the completed and limit isomorphisms, apply the ordinary cone square, and use naturality of the ordinary-to-derived limit map. The varying single-object adjunct identity and inverse cancellation yield the required pre-varying equality.

proof_origin.place: paragraph (2), ordinary coefficient cone compatibility followed by full derived normalization
